text: A man spent three days inside a fish, and he got there by running from God.
God told Jonah to go to Nineveh, the enemy's great city, and warn it. Jonah bought a ticket going the opposite way.
Out at sea, a storm hit so hard the sailors each cried out to their own god. Jonah was asleep below deck.
They cast lots, and the lot fell on Jonah. “Throw me into the sea,” he said, “and it will calm.”
They did. The sea went still. And a great fish swallowed him.
For three days and three nights, Jonah prayed in the dark.
Then the fish spat him out onto dry land.
So he walked into Nineveh and said one sentence: “40 days, and Nineveh will be overthrown.”
The whole city believed. Even the king sat down in ashes. And God spared them. Here’s the twist.
Jonah was furious. He’d run away because he knew God was merciful.
So God asked him, “Shouldn’t I care about a city of 120,000 people?” And the book ends on that question.
